summary.one_liner: A 2016 SREcon Europe conference talk by Greg Veith of Microsoft on building SRE culture and practices within Azure, drawing on lessons from Bing.
use_cases: Learning how a large enterprise moves toward SRE practices
Comparing Bing's operational experience with Azure's SRE build-out
Understanding cultural change needed to adopt DevOps and SRE
Reference reading for SRE teams planning organizational change
summary.what_it_does: The page is the abstract and speaker bio for a talk at USENIX SREcon16 Europe in Dublin. The talk describes how Microsoft is shifting toward SRE, arguing that it requires cultural engineering as well as technical investment. It compares the journey within Bing, a cloud-born service with about 13 years of experience, to the current state of SRE within Microsoft Azure. The speaker is Greg Veith, Director of the Azure Site Reliability Engineering team. The page does not include slides, video, or a full transcript.
notable: Compares Bing's 13 years of cloud-scale operations with Azure's SRE build-out
Speaker leads the Azure Site Reliability Engineering team at Microsoft
Hosted by USENIX as part of SREcon16 Europe, Dublin
caveats: Only the abstract and bio are available; no slides, recording, or transcript are shown on the page
Talk is from 2016 and describes Microsoft's SRE state at that time
